position_a: Always target -18 dBFS for every plug-in
position_b: Use each plug-in’s documented reference/headroom and desired nonlinear response
what_decides: Product calibration, source dynamics, and whether the processor is linear or nonlinear decide.

position_a: Set every track by peak level
position_b: Use average/RMS/VU-like level for some calibration decisions and preserve peak headroom
what_decides: Source crest factor and the processor’s detector/reference decide.

position_a: Record as close to 0 dBFS as possible
position_b: Leave generous converter headroom in 24-bit recording
what_decides: Real noise floor, performance unpredictability, and hardware decide.

position_a: Use the channel fader for every gain problem
position_b: Use region/trim/input controls when downstream processing must react differently
what_decides: Whether the change should affect inserts, sends, or only mix balance decides.

position_a: Any red internal meter means irreversible clipping
position_b: Floating-point internal stages may exceed 0 dBFS without sample clipping
what_decides: The exact stage, plug-in, bounce, converter, and output format decide.

position_a: Pull down only the final output to create headroom
position_b: Reduce the earliest overloaded nonlinear/summing stage when needed
what_decides: Whether intermediate processors are being overdriven decides.

position_a: Keep all analog-modeled plug-ins at low level to stay clean
position_b: Drive some models intentionally for color
what_decides: The model’s calibration, headroom control, noise, and artistic goal decide.

position_a: Always meter pre-fader
position_b: Use post-fader metering for mix balance and pre-fader for source/input questions
what_decides: The question being asked decides.

position_a: Always level before compression
position_b: Use post-compressor level when only final balance should change
what_decides: Whether detector behavior should change decides.

position_a: Normalize every imported file before mixing
position_b: Use intentional trim/region gain and preserve source relationships
what_decides: Source consistency, workflow, and processor calibration decide.

position_a: Leave instrument outputs at maximum and use faders
position_b: Reduce overly hot instrument output before downstream processing
what_decides: Preset design, nonlinear inserts, and fader resolution decide.

position_a: A mix must peak exactly -6 dBFS for mastering
position_b: Deliver unclipped, sensible, documented headroom without chasing one number
what_decides: Mastering workflow and absence of damaging processing decide.

position_a: Use DAW dBFS values as direct analog dBu values
position_b: Calibrate converter/hardware reference explicitly
what_decides: Interface headroom, nominal levels, and device specifications decide.

position_a: Use Auto Gain for fair comparisons
position_b: Match output manually or verify auto-gain behavior
what_decides: Whether auto gain is accurate and program-independent enough decides.

position_a: Use a send to create every subgroup
position_b: Route outputs to an aux for true subgrouping; use sends for parallel paths
what_decides: Whether dry signal should continue separately decides.

position_a: Folder and Summing Stacks are interchangeable
position_b: Summing Stacks route audio to a subgroup; Folder Stacks organize/control differently
what_decides: Whether shared audio processing is required decides.

position_a: Use an aux whenever one fader should control tracks
position_b: Use a VCA when control is needed without audio summing
what_decides: Signal-flow and post-fader send behavior decide.

position_a: Every family needs bus processing
position_b: Use a bus only when shared routing/control/processing serves the mix
what_decides: Audible benefit and workflow clarity decide.

position_a: A compressor automatically glues a bus
position_b: Shared gain movement can cohere or flatten
what_decides: Detector behavior, timing, amount, and arrangement decide.

position_a: Fix family tone only on the bus
position_b: Fix one offending member at the source when appropriate
what_decides: Whether the tendency is truly shared decides.

position_a: Parallel processing sounds better because it is denser
position_b: Level-match total output before judging
what_decides: Whether added level or actual processing creates the preference decides.

position_a: Route every drum-related channel through one bus
position_b: Exclude or separately route rooms, parallel paths, or effects when needed
what_decides: Detector control, phase, and creative role decide.

position_a: Put lead, doubles, harmonies, and ad-libs through identical processing
position_b: Use separate subgroups when hierarchy or processing needs differ
what_decides: Lead stability and stack role decide.

position_a: More bus stages always improve organization
position_b: Keep hierarchy only as deep as necessary
what_decides: Routing clarity, latency, automation ownership, and troubleshooting decide.

position_a: Drive the bus until it sounds exciting in solo
position_b: Judge nonlinear bus color in the full mix at matched loudness
what_decides: Cumulative intermodulation, harshness, and headroom decide.

position_a: Always mix into bus processing from the start
position_b: Add it later and rebalance if that workflow serves the project
what_decides: Workflow, intent, and how much the mix adapts to processing decide.

position_a: Use LUFS to prevent clipping
position_b: Use peak/true-peak metering for clipping and LUFS for loudness
what_decides: The measurement goal decides.

position_a: RMS and LUFS are interchangeable
position_b: LUFS uses standardized weighting/gating and programme windows
what_decides: Delivery and comparison requirements decide.

position_a: Use integrated LUFS on a chorus loop as the song value
position_b: Measure integrated over the intended full programme
what_decides: Measurement duration and programme scope decide.

position_a: Higher or lower LRA is inherently better
position_b: Treat LRA as descriptive programme variation
what_decides: Genre, arrangement, playback, and artistic intent decide.

position_a: True-peak limiting must always be enabled
position_b: Use it when delivery/reconstruction risk matters and audition the result
what_decides: Destination, codec, ceiling, and transient tradeoff decide.

position_a: Set every limiter ceiling to 0 dBFS
position_b: Leave context-appropriate true-peak margin when needed
what_decides: Delivery format and true-peak behavior decide.

position_a: A limiter always fixes peaks safely at the end
position_b: Control problematic sources/arrangement before final limiting
what_decides: Whether a few upstream events dominate gain reduction decides.

position_a: Clipping is always harsher than limiting
position_b: Small controlled clipping can preserve different transients than limiting
what_decides: Material, transfer curve, oversampling, and amount decide.

position_a: Soft clipping is transparent
position_b: Soft clipping still changes waveform, harmonics, and peaks
what_decides: Amount and source spectrum decide.

position_a: Master every song to -14 LUFS for streaming
position_b: Master for sound and delivery; normalization is playback gain management
what_decides: Platform behavior, genre, album intent, and quality decide.

position_a: A louder unnormalized master is better
position_b: Compare at matched playback loudness
what_decides: Transient quality, distortion, and artistic intent decide.

position_a: High crest factor is always punchier
position_b: Crest factor is context/window dependent and source-specific
what_decides: Envelope, arrangement, and playback decide.

position_a: One dynamic-range number defines musical dynamics
position_b: Use several measurements plus listening over appropriate windows
what_decides: Transient, macro contrast, and programme duration decide.

position_a: Use a faster limiter to handle bass pumping
position_b: Fix source envelope, level, or arrangement when low end dominates
what_decides: Cause of gain reduction and desired bass weight decide.

position_a: One limiter is always cleaner than several stages
position_b: Several gentle stages can distribute work, but also accumulate artifacts
what_decides: Algorithm, stage amount, and level matching decide.

position_a: Clipper-before-limiter gives free loudness
position_b: It trades one type of peak control/distortion for another
what_decides: Material and total artifact budget decide.

position_a: Normalize every track independently to one loudness
position_b: Preserve intentional album-level relationships when appropriate
what_decides: Release format and album intent decide.

position_a: Only final-meter readings matter
position_b: Use stage meters to diagnose and final meters for delivery
what_decides: Whether the task is diagnosis or compliance decides.

position_a: Keep a mastering limiter active while every mix decision is made
position_b: Use it intentionally and verify that it is not hiding balance/transient problems
what_decides: Workflow and amount of limiting decide.

position_a: Mastering engineers require exactly one peak number
position_b: They require unclipped, unprocessed-or-documented files with useful margin
what_decides: The specific mastering relationship and file format decide.

position_a: A loudness penalty means the master failed
position_b: Normalization gain does not directly measure quality
what_decides: Audible quality after matched playback decides.

position_a: Yellow or red meter color alone proves damage
position_b: Meter colors are warnings; actual stage behavior and sustained overload matter
what_decides: The meter mode and stage decide.
